title: MAX-DESIGN decision catalog
description: Original, locally searchable MAX-DESIGN decision guidance for product profiles, visual direction, page patterns, interactions, density, color, typography, motion, UX quality, charts, and implementation stacks.
guidance: Inspect the product and current codebase before selecting a direction. Match patterns to the user's task, available evidence, and constraints. See docs/decision-framework.md.

directions.title: Editorial clarity
directions.summary: Type-led layouts for content-rich products where comprehension and expertise matter.
fitWhen: Content is the main product value
Users need to scan, compare, or read deeply
layout: Use a controlled reading measure and visible heading hierarchy
Use grids only when they help comparison or browsing
directions.typography: Use a restrained type system with obvious heading and body roles; validate line length and text resizing.
directions.colorApproach: Use a deliberate neutral base and a small semantic accent; preserve readable contrast.
signature: Strong typographic rhythm
Purposeful rules, indices, captions, or editorial alignment
avoid: Making every section a boxed card
Oversized headings that crowd actual content
risks: Long titles and translations may alter the composition
Thin or decorative type can fail at small sizes

directions.title: Calm enterprise
directions.summary: Predictable and trustworthy interfaces for complex workflows, settings, and business tools.
fitWhen: Users perform repeated operational tasks
Auditability and low ambiguity matter
layout: Group by task and show related controls together
Make primary, secondary, and destructive actions visually distinct
directions.typography: Prioritize legible text, tabular numeric alignment where useful, and stable hierarchy.
directions.colorApproach: Use semantic roles for surfaces, text, borders, focus, and status instead of using brand color everywhere.
signature: Clear active navigation
Quiet but explicit status and focus treatment
avoid: Making all actions equally prominent
Generic grey cards with no information hierarchy
risks: Dense tables require responsive and zoom testing

directions.title: Technical instrument
directions.summary: Information-dense interfaces for monitoring, developer tools, and analytical work.
fitWhen: Users monitor changing values or investigate anomalies
High information density is useful to the target audience
layout: Prioritize changes, thresholds, and actionable anomalies
Use persistent metric names, units, filters, and freshness indicators
directions.typography: Favor high legibility and stable numeral treatment; never shrink labels simply to fit more cards.
directions.colorApproach: Reserve vivid status colors for consistent meanings and pair them with text or icons.
signature: Useful comparison views
Compact but well-labeled instrumentation
avoid: Neon decoration unrelated to a state
Charts without definitions, ranges, or source context
risks: Dense views can overwhelm novice users
Streaming data and large tables may hurt performance

directions.title: Warm guidance
directions.summary: Supportive product flows for onboarding, setup, learning, and help-oriented tasks.
fitWhen: Users are new to the product or task
Confidence and recoverability matter
layout: Break the task into understandable chunks
Show helpful next steps and preserve context across steps
directions.typography: Use direct labels, clear instructions, and comfortable body text.
directions.colorApproach: Use restrained warmth as a supporting tone; retain strong contrast and clear status roles.
signature: Helpful inline examples
Progress that represents real steps or actual work
avoid: Forced product tours
Cheerful copy that hides errors or consequences
risks: Long steps create scroll burden on mobile
Progress indicators can mislead if work is not linear

directions.title: Expressive brand
directions.summary: Memorable visual systems for creative, cultural, or consumer brands where identity is part of the value.
fitWhen: Brand expression is an explicit product goal
The audience and task can support a distinctive composition
layout: Select one focal point and let supporting content recede
Use contrast, scale, or asymmetry intentionally
directions.typography: Use expressive display type only when body copy remains highly readable.
directions.colorApproach: Choose a small, intentional palette with semantic status and accessible interaction states.
signature: A product-specific composition or art direction
Meaningful imagery or graphic motifs
avoid: Stacking every effect at once
Animation or contrast that competes with primary actions
risks: Large type and asymmetry can fail at narrow widths
Brand colors may fail contrast for controls or text

directions.title: Commerce confidence
directions.summary: Product discovery and purchase flows that help people evaluate choices and understand cost, availability, and next steps.
fitWhen: Users browse, compare, select, or buy items
Transparent details and predictable next steps build trust
layout: Make product identity, price, availability, and relevant differences easy to scan
Keep filters and selected options visible and reversible
directions.typography: Keep prices, quantities, units, and option labels unambiguous.
directions.colorApproach: Use clear selection and availability states; never rely on color alone.
signature: Useful product comparisons
Clear selected, unavailable, and confirmation states
avoid: Invented reviews, urgency, scarcity, or social proof
Surprise fees or hidden selection state
risks: Variant and price data must remain consistent across states

pagePatterns.title: SaaS landing page
pagePatterns.summary: Explain value quickly, establish credible proof, show how the product works, then present a clear next action.
pagePatterns.question: Who is this for, what outcome does it create, and why should the visitor believe it?
priorities: Specific headline and supporting sentence
Product evidence or a real use-case demonstration
One clear primary CTA with a predictable destination
Important objections, limits, or pricing context where relevant
states: Consent or preference state if present
antiPatterns: Generic claims like best-in-class with no evidence
Repeated feature cards with indistinguishable hierarchy

pagePatterns.title: Analytics dashboard
pagePatterns.summary: Turn measurements into a decision rather than presenting a wall of equally weighted cards.
pagePatterns.question: What changed, compared with what, and what should the user do next?
priorities: Metric definitions, units, and time range
Data freshness and current filters
A hierarchy that distinguishes critical signals from context
Chart choice matched to the decision
states: No data and no filter matches
antiPatterns: Decorative charts with no decision value

pagePatterns.title: Data management table
pagePatterns.summary: Help users find, compare, and act on records while preserving context and preventing accidental changes.
pagePatterns.question: How does a person find the right record and understand the effect of an action?
priorities: Clear column labels and meaningful sort behavior
Search, filters, and active filter summary
Selection and bulk-action scope
Responsive fallback for wide data
antiPatterns: Tiny text instead of adapting the layout

pagePatterns.title: Settings and admin
pagePatterns.summary: Make configuration discoverable, changes understandable, and destructive operations safe.
pagePatterns.question: Can users locate a setting, understand its current value, and safely change it?
priorities: Task-based grouping and local navigation
Explanatory labels for consequential options
Visible saved/unsaved state
Permission and reset behavior
antiPatterns: Destructive reset beside routine controls without distinction

pagePatterns.title: Form and onboarding flow
pagePatterns.summary: Help users submit accurate information with minimal unnecessary effort and recoverable errors.
pagePatterns.question: What is the minimum necessary data, and how can a user correct mistakes without losing work?
priorities: Persistent labels and useful examples
Necessary fields only
Clear validation timing and correction guidance
Server response and success confirmation
antiPatterns: Fake success when no submission succeeded

pagePatterns.title: Search and empty states
pagePatterns.summary: Help users recover when content is absent, a filter is too narrow, or a search query has no match.
pagePatterns.question: Why is there no content, and what is the next useful action?
priorities: Distinguish genuinely empty from filter mismatch
Preserve query and selected filters
Offer relevant reset, retry, or create action
Make errors separate from no-results
antiPatterns: Same empty message for every cause
Fake content presented as live results

interactionPatterns.title: Asynchronous save
interactionPatterns.summary: Communicate pending and confirmed save state without implying success prematurely.
behavior: Show pending feedback on the affected control or region
Prevent duplicate submission if it would create harmful duplicate work
Confirm success only after the system confirms it
On failure, preserve safe input and explain retry or correction

interactionPatterns.title: Destructive action guard
interactionPatterns.summary: Make irreversible consequences clear without adding pointless confirmation friction to routine work.
behavior: Use an explicit verb naming the target or consequence
Keep destructive and routine actions visually distinct
Require confirmation when risk justifies it; provide undo when feasible
Explain what cannot be restored

interactionPatterns.title: Filter and search state
interactionPatterns.summary: Keep search, active filters, result counts, and empty states synchronized and recoverable.
behavior: Represent active filters so users can review and remove them
Preserve query when details or pagination are revisited when appropriate
Debounce only where it improves behavior and expose loading state when delay matters
Differentiate no data from no matches

interactionPatterns.title: Dialog and overlay
interactionPatterns.summary: Keep modal context, keyboard focus, and dismissal behavior predictable.
behavior: Give the dialog a programmatic name
Move focus in and return focus logically on close
Support Escape for dismissible dialogs and make dismissal rules clear
Prevent background interaction only when the dialog is truly modal

interactionPatterns.title: Meaningful loading and empty states
interactionPatterns.summary: Show accurate status and a helpful next step without fabricating progress or results.
behavior: Use skeletons when they reduce perceived structural shift, not as decoration
Use determinate progress only when progress can be measured
Explain what is missing and the next useful action in an empty state
Distinguish stale, partial, and failed data when the difference matters

densityProfiles.title: Spacious
densityProfiles.summary: Emphasize focus and readability for low-density tasks and content-led pages.
useWhen: Few high-value actions or content elements
Users need to read or decide without distraction
layoutRules: Use a clear content width and visible grouping
cautions: Do not waste space on operational screens where comparison matters

densityProfiles.title: Balanced
densityProfiles.summary: Support mixed content, actions, and context without overwhelming the page.
useWhen: A page combines summary and a handful of actions
A broad audience needs scanability and breathing room
layoutRules: Group related details and collapse only secondary complexity
cautions: Avoid applying the same card grid to every section

densityProfiles.title: Compact
densityProfiles.summary: Support expert workflows and high-volume information while retaining legible controls.
useWhen: Users compare many records or act repeatedly
Information density is a real task requirement
layoutRules: Use clear alignment and stable labels
Preserve sorting, focus, spacing, and status meaning
cautions: Do not shrink text and targets as the only means of fitting more content

productProfiles.title: AI SaaS product
productProfiles.summary: Design AI products around useful outcomes, trust, controllability, and clear limits—not a chat box with decorative gradients.
fitWhen: The product generates, summarizes, classifies, or transforms user content
Users need to understand model capability, cost, privacy, and uncertainty
priorities: Make the primary task and expected output clear before asking for a prompt
Show generation state, partial results, failure, retry, stop, and edit/regenerate controls
Separate model output from verified facts and label sources where available
Explain data retention and external processing where applicable
avoid: Invented accuracy badges or unsupported model claims
Infinite chat as the only information architecture
Hiding latency, limits, credits, or destructive consequences

productProfiles.title: AI conversation workspace
productProfiles.summary: Treat conversation as a work surface with history, context, artifact editing, and recovery.
priorities: Preserve user input after errors and allow cancellation
Distinguish user messages, model output, tool activity, and cited sources
Provide useful empty-state examples without pretending they are real conversations
Keep long output readable with copy, regenerate, and navigation affordances
avoid: Autoscrolling when a user is reviewing older content
Showing tool success before the tool confirms it
Unlabeled controls represented only by icons

productProfiles.title: Developer tool or API platform
productProfiles.summary: Optimize technical confidence, discoverability, copyable examples, and fast feedback.
priorities: Put the common task and working example before exhaustive reference material
Make code, status, errors, scopes, and environment distinctions explicit
Keep navigation, search, version selection, and copy feedback predictable
Provide safe sandbox or preview behavior when the product supports it
avoid: Marketing language in operational controls
Code examples that omit required context or error handling
Color-only status or uncopyable long tokens

productProfiles.title: E-commerce catalog
productProfiles.summary: Help shoppers narrow a large inventory without losing context or creating accidental purchases.
priorities: Use meaningful category, price, availability, and attribute filters
Keep applied filters visible and removable; show result counts when reliable
Preserve sort and filter state during back navigation
Use product photography consistently and reserve space to avoid layout shifts
avoid: Filters that silently reset on navigation
Fake scarcity, countdowns, ratings, or inventory
Hover-only product actions on touch devices

productProfiles.title: Product detail and purchase flow
productProfiles.summary: Make product suitability, total cost, variants, availability, and purchase consequences easy to evaluate.
priorities: Show price, essential options, availability, delivery/returns, and primary action in a clear order
Make variant selection affect the displayed product state accurately
Validate cart changes and surface asynchronous success or failure
Keep checkout progress, totals, and editable details visible
avoid: Hiding fees until the last step
Using a disabled button without explaining what is missing
Treating a click as confirmation before the server responds

productProfiles.title: Analytics or operations dashboard
productProfiles.summary: Make status and change over time legible before adding visual density.
priorities: Choose a small set of decision-driving summary metrics
State time range, timezone, filters, freshness, and units near the data
Provide drill-down from aggregate to supporting detail
Design loading, stale, partial, no-data, and failed-query states
avoid: Decorative chart walls with no decisions attached
Comparing incompatible time windows or units
Red/green status without text or shape cues

productProfiles.title: Editorial or documentation site
productProfiles.summary: Support reading, search, deep linking, and hierarchy for long-form information.
priorities: Use a comfortable reading measure, descriptive headings, and scannable sections
Keep tables of contents and article navigation predictable
Distinguish examples, warnings, notes, and quotations semantically
Preserve heading order and anchor links for deep linking
avoid: Tiny gray body text or unnecessarily wide paragraphs
Using cards for every paragraph
Interactive content that blocks ordinary reading or browser navigation

productProfiles.title: Portfolio and case-study site
productProfiles.summary: Show the work, constraints, decisions, and outcomes with visual confidence and restrained storytelling.
priorities: Lead with a clear role and relevant work sample
Explain problem, constraints, contribution, process, and verifiable result
Give images useful alt text and preserve readable captions
Provide a clear contact or next-step path
avoid: Unsupported client logos or performance claims
Animation that delays access to the work
Same generic grid for every project regardless of content

productProfiles.title: Booking and appointment flow
productProfiles.summary: Help users choose a valid option, understand availability, confirm details, and recover from conflicts.
priorities: Keep timezone, duration, location, and selected date explicit
Distinguish unavailable, loading, held, pending, and confirmed states
Preserve completed fields when availability changes
Summarize the booking and cancellation terms before final submission
avoid: Assuming local time without labeling it
Showing a success screen before confirmation
Clearing the whole flow after one unavailable slot

productProfiles.title: Learning and education interface
productProfiles.summary: Support focus, progress comprehension, useful feedback, and low-friction return to unfinished work.
priorities: Show course structure, current position, and a clear next step
Distinguish attempted, completed, graded, and saved states
Provide actionable feedback rather than only right/wrong color
Support keyboard navigation, captions, and flexible text sizes
avoid: Using streaks or notifications to obscure learning goals
Locking essential explanation behind motion
Confusing viewed content with mastered content

productProfiles.title: Financial or money-management interface
productProfiles.summary: Prioritize accurate amounts, clear units, transparent assumptions, and deliberate high-impact actions.
priorities: Format currency and dates consistently and state the period covered
Explain calculations and distinguish estimates from confirmed values
Require clear confirmation for transfers, deletes, and other consequential actions
Make empty, pending, reversed, failed, and completed transactions distinct
avoid: Color-only gains/losses
Invented financial performance or account activity
Ambiguous totals that mix pending and settled amounts

styleDirections.title: Quiet minimalism
styleDirections.summary: Use a reduced visual vocabulary, strong alignment, and precise type to make the task feel calm and focused.
fitWhen: The content or workflow is the primary value
Frequent use requires low visual fatigue
signature: One clear hierarchy per viewport
Restrained borders and a consistent spacing scale
Color reserved for actions and semantic status
implementation: Use a neutral surface foundation and a single controlled accent
Use alignment and spacing before shadows to group content
avoid: Mistaking emptiness for hierarchy
Removing affordances or focus indicators to achieve a sparse look

styleDirections.title: Editorial premium
styleDirections.summary: Use expressive typography, deliberate image cropping, and controlled asymmetry to create a considered magazine-like experience.
fitWhen: The brand depends on authorship, craft, or a curated point of view
Images and stories are important purchase or exploration cues
signature: Distinct display and reading type roles
Whitespace with clear caption and metadata styles
A limited, well-controlled image art direction
avoid: Low-contrast thin type
Asymmetry that damages mobile reading order
Treating every heading as a billboard

styleDirections.title: Technical instrument
styleDirections.summary: Make dense capability feel precise with tabular data, monospaced accents, restrained surfaces, and explicit status.
fitWhen: Users monitor systems, inspect logs, or configure advanced tools
signature: Aligned numeric columns and clear units
Consistent status tokens and focus states
Compact but readable control groups
avoid: Monospaced body text everywhere
Glow effects that compete with data
Dense screens without sorting, filtering, or keyboard support

styleDirections.title: Warm and human
styleDirections.summary: Use warmer neutrals, organic imagery, friendly language, and generous rhythm without sacrificing precision.
fitWhen: The product needs approachability, reassurance, or a human voice
signature: Warm neutral canvas with one grounded accent
Human, direct labels and non-judgmental error text
Natural imagery used with a clear content purpose
avoid: Pastel-on-pastel text
Overusing rounded pills and soft shadows
Infantilizing language for adult or professional users

styleDirections.title: Bold constructive contrast
styleDirections.summary: Use strong typography, visible structure, and decisive blocks as an intentional brand system—not as an excuse to ignore usability.
fitWhen: The brand benefits from a distinctive editorial or cultural voice
signature: A deliberately limited high-contrast palette
A clear grid with intentionally bold breaks
Visible button and link affordances
avoid: Broken layout disguised as experimentation
Low legibility, hover-only actions, or accidental horizontal overflow

styleDirections.title: Layered translucent surfaces
styleDirections.summary: Use translucency to show depth and context sparingly, particularly for overlays floating above stable content.
fitWhen: A small number of overlays need visual separation from a rich background
signature: Opaque fallback surface behind translucent layers
Subtle boundary and clear elevation order
Foreground contrast tested on the brightest background region
avoid: Using blur as the primary hierarchy tool
Applying translucent cards to all content
Depending on backdrop-filter without a fallback

styleDirections.title: Dark technical workspace
styleDirections.summary: Use deep neutral surfaces and differentiated elevation for prolonged, data-rich work where a dark theme is appropriate.
fitWhen: The target environment or user preference benefits from a dark workspace
signature: Several distinguishable surface levels without pure-black everywhere
Readable muted text and clearly visible keyboard focus
Status colors tuned for the dark background
avoid: Neon glow around every control
Low-contrast gray metadata
Assuming dark mode alone improves accessibility or battery life

styleDirections.title: Motion-led storytelling
styleDirections.summary: Use staged transitions to explain sequence, reveal spatial relationships, or guide attention through a narrative.
fitWhen: Sequence or spatial continuity helps explain the content
signature: Motion connected to an explicit user or narrative purpose
Small, interruptible transitions with meaningful resting states
Reduced-motion behavior that preserves content order
avoid: Continuous movement behind text
Scroll hijacking or delayed primary content
Animating many unrelated elements simultaneously

colorStrategies.title: Trustworthy enterprise palette
colorStrategies.summary: A restrained blue-and-neutral foundation with clear semantic status roles for dependable business software.
fitWhen: The product is data-heavy, operational, or professional
priorities: Use primary blue for the main action and active navigation, not every decoration
Reserve green, amber, and red for consistent status meanings
Test all text and focus combinations on actual surfaces
avoid: Making every link, card, chart, and status the same blue
Using muted text below readable contrast

colorStrategies.title: Direct commerce palette
colorStrategies.summary: A stable neutral product canvas with one high-contrast purchase action and a small set of clear status colors.
fitWhen: Product photography, price, and variant information should dominate
priorities: Keep CTA color and wording consistent through product and checkout steps
Ensure sale labels do not overwhelm product information
Show discounts and totals as actual calculations
avoid: Urgency colors used for false scarcity
Multiple competing CTA colors on a single decision

colorStrategies.title: Warm editorial palette
colorStrategies.summary: Cream-like backgrounds, dark ink, and a restrained earthy accent create a curated reading or premium retail mood.
fitWhen: The brand depends on considered content, materials, or craft
priorities: Keep long-form text dark enough for reading
Use the earthy accent for links, selection, or small emphasis
Keep imagery and surface tones consistent across the site
avoid: Low-contrast tan text on cream
Treating every surface as the same shade with no hierarchy

colorStrategies.title: Dark workspace palette
colorStrategies.summary: Use dark navy and slate surfaces with light text and restrained bright accents for a readable technical environment.
fitWhen: A user-selected or environment-appropriate dark theme is required
priorities: Test muted text, charts, focus rings, and disabled states independently
Use surface differences and borders rather than glow to show grouping
Provide a matching light theme when user or product requirements call for one
avoid: Assuming colors accessible on white remain accessible on dark surfaces
Using saturated accents for all elements

colorStrategies.title: Calm wellbeing palette
colorStrategies.summary: A muted teal or green with bright neutral surfaces can signal reassurance while keeping controls and information clear.
fitWhen: The product benefits from a calm and supportive tone
priorities: Use reassuring wording and clear next steps alongside color
Make medical or important alerts unmistakable even within a calm theme
Validate contrast for small labels and form feedback
avoid: Pastel-only status distinctions
Soft color being used to hide important risk information

colorStrategies.title: Semantic multi-state system
colorStrategies.summary: Choose colors by role and meaning so status, selected state, and actions remain consistent across the entire product.
priorities: Define roles for text, surface, border, action, focus, success, warning, error, and informational states
Pair color with text or icon shape for non-decorative status
Check each role in all supported themes and component states
avoid: Red/green as the only difference between states
Raw one-off hex values scattered through components
Assuming palette names prove WCAG conformance

typographySystems.title: Modern product typography
typographySystems.summary: A neutral sans-serif family with a clear size and weight scale supports interface controls, navigation, and product content.
typographySystems.pairing: Inter or system UI for both headings and body; use weight, size, and spacing to create roles.
fitWhen: The interface has many controls and mixed content types
priorities: Define semantic display, heading, body, label, helper, and numeric roles
Use a readable body baseline near 16 CSS px where the context permits
Keep line height and measure comfortable for real content
avoid: Using weight and color alone for every level of hierarchy
Loading many font files for minimal benefit

typographySystems.title: Technical heading and body pairing
typographySystems.summary: A distinctive heading face can give a developer product character while a highly readable body face remains quiet.
typographySystems.pairing: A display face such as Space Grotesk for short headings plus a neutral sans such as Inter or DM Sans for body and controls.
fitWhen: Brand distinction matters but technical detail must remain readable
priorities: Keep long code, logs, and numeric values in appropriate monospace roles
Check fallback font metrics to avoid layout jumps
Use font features and weights consistently
avoid: Using display type for paragraphs or form labels
Relying on a hosted font without system fallback

typographySystems.title: Editorial reading system
typographySystems.summary: A readable serif for long-form expression paired with a neutral sans-serif for navigation and controls creates a clear content/utility distinction.
typographySystems.pairing: Source Serif 4 or a similar text serif for editorial content with a neutral sans-serif such as Inter for UI controls.
fitWhen: Articles, essays, documentation, or stories are central
priorities: Test paragraph density, punctuation, italics, captions, and footnotes
Keep navigation and controls unambiguous
Set measure and line height for comfortable reading
avoid: Tiny footnotes for essential content
Low-contrast thin serif styles on mobile screens

typographySystems.title: Refined display typography
typographySystems.summary: A high-character display face can communicate craft when paired with simpler supporting text and restrained styling.
typographySystems.pairing: A display serif such as Fraunces or Cormorant Garamond for short headings with a neutral sans such as Manrope or Inter for body text.
fitWhen: Visual identity and editorial atmosphere are key brand signals
priorities: Limit the decorative family to clear display roles
Check headings at narrow widths and increased text size
Use a robust fallback and avoid blocking first render
avoid: Using thin display weights for functional text
Making every heading oversized

typographySystems.title: Friendly service typography
typographySystems.summary: Open, approachable letterforms and a moderate weight scale support forms, help text, and public-facing services.
typographySystems.pairing: A neutral humanist sans or system UI family used with a restrained weight scale and generous line height.
fitWhen: Users need reassurance and quick comprehension
priorities: Prioritize letter clarity in labels and numerical fields
Use sentence case and predictable emphasis
Test localization and 200% text zoom
avoid: Tiny all-caps labels for important information
Overusing rounded display fonts that reduce information density

typographySystems.title: Data and code typography
typographySystems.summary: Use tabular numerals and a consistent monospace role where exact alignment or source-code recognition improves scanning.
priorities: Enable tabular numerals for columns of comparable values where supported
Differentiate code from prose without making code too small
Show units and precision consistently
avoid: Using monospace for every heading and body paragraph
Aligning data with repeated spaces instead of layout primitives

motionRecipes.title: Control feedback
motionRecipes.summary: A brief transform or color response should make activation feel acknowledged without interrupting the task.
behavior: Use opacity, color, or a very small transform for hover and press feedback
Return to the resting state reliably on pointer leave and keyboard blur
Keep the actual action synchronous with the input semantics
priorities: Support hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, and touch behavior as relevant
avoid: Moving controls out of reach
Motion that is the only sign of selection or activation

motionRecipes.title: Section reveal
motionRecipes.summary: Use a subtle reveal only when it helps establish sequence or emphasize sections without hiding meaningful content.
behavior: Prefer opacity and transform to layout-changing properties
Ensure content remains available when JavaScript or motion is unavailable
Observe reduced-motion preferences and render the final state directly
avoid: Delaying above-the-fold content
Replaying every element on each tiny scroll movement

motionRecipes.title: Dialog and overlay transition
motionRecipes.summary: A short opacity and scale transition can clarify an overlay entering or leaving while preserving focus and dismissal behavior.
behavior: Animate the overlay and dialog with a clear shared timing
Move focus into the dialog and restore it to the trigger after close
Keep Escape, explicit close, and permitted backdrop behavior predictable
avoid: Animating past the point where the dialog is interactive
Closing a form on a backdrop click without protecting user input

motionRecipes.title: Loading and progress
motionRecipes.summary: Show activity when work is genuinely pending and use determinate progress only when progress can be measured.
behavior: For very short actions, prefer a clear pending label or button state
Use skeletons when the incoming content structure is known
Use determinate progress only when the value reflects actual work
priorities: Keep previous user input and stable layout when appropriate
Provide cancellation for long-running cancellable work
avoid: Fake percentage progress
Spinners that continue after failure or completion

motionRecipes.title: Success confirmation
motionRecipes.summary: A brief, non-blocking confirmation should tell users what completed and what they can do next.
motionRecipes.duration: Usually 150–250 ms for the visual transition; message persistence depends on importance.
behavior: Announce important status changes accessibly
Use text and optional icon along with semantic color
Provide an undo path when reversal is safe and useful
avoid: Auto-dismissing critical information too quickly
Animating success before the system confirms completion

motionRecipes.title: Data and chart transition
motionRecipes.summary: Animate changes only when movement helps explain the relationship between two valid data states.
behavior: Use a stable scale and consistent mapping between old and new values
Keep labels and tooltips synchronized with the current data
Turn off or shorten movement for reduced-motion preferences
avoid: Racing charts, perpetual loops, and motion that exaggerates differences
Animating every datapoint when updates are frequent

motionRecipes.title: Drag and reorder feedback
motionRecipes.summary: Make the drop target, current position, and final result obvious; provide a non-drag alternative when the task matters.
behavior: Show a clear insertion indicator and selected item state
Support keyboard or explicit move-up/move-down alternatives where appropriate
Persist the resulting order only after the interaction is accepted
avoid: Relying on pointer movement alone
Using animation that hides the final location or changes the data silently

motionRecipes.title: Reduced-motion behavior
motionRecipes.summary: Motion must degrade to a usable static or low-motion experience without removing information or functionality.
behavior: Respect prefers-reduced-motion for non-essential motion
Remove parallax, large spatial transitions, and automatic looping when reduction is requested
Preserve state changes, progress, and content without animation
priorities: Test the reduced-motion experience, not only the default animation
avoid: Applying a global duration of zero when important feedback would disappear
Making content invisible until an animation fires

uxGuidelines.title: Contrast and semantic color
uxGuidelines.summary: Choose foreground and background pairs by actual contrast and reserve semantic colors for stable meanings.
do: Target at least 4.5:1 contrast for normal text and 3:1 for qualifying large text
Check focus indicators, disabled states, placeholder text, chart labels, and dark mode separately
Use labels or icon/shape cues alongside important colors
avoid: Assuming palette swatches are accessible as text/background pairs
Using color alone for errors, success, or chart series
verify: Measure actual rendered pairs and test forced-colors or high-contrast contexts where relevant

uxGuidelines.title: Keyboard and focus
uxGuidelines.summary: Every interactive control needs a predictable keyboard path and a visible focus state.
do: Use native semantics for buttons, links, fields, and dialogs
Ensure focus remains visible and unobscured
Return focus to a logical location after overlay workflows
avoid: Removing outlines without an equally visible replacement
Positive tabindex values and keyboard traps
verify: Complete the primary journey without a pointer

uxGuidelines.title: Touch target and spacing
uxGuidelines.summary: Provide adequately sized, separated targets for touch input while respecting dense desktop workflows.
do: Use the target platform's accessibility guidance; aim around 44 by 44 CSS px for common touch controls where practical
Separate destructive and primary actions
Provide visible pressed and disabled feedback
avoid: Tiny adjacent icon-only buttons
Hover-only menus or tooltips
verify: Test the smallest supported viewport and touch interaction

uxGuidelines.title: Form labels and validation
uxGuidelines.summary: Help people understand a field before entry, then identify and correct errors close to where they occur.
do: Use persistent labels and explain required formats before submission when possible
Associate errors and help text with their fields
Preserve valid input and provide a specific recovery instruction
avoid: Placeholder-only labels
Clearing a whole form after a correctable error
Showing an error only by changing border color
verify: Test empty, malformed, server-rejected, and corrected submissions

uxGuidelines.title: Asynchronous state integrity
uxGuidelines.summary: Make pending, success, failure, retry, and cancellation distinct and grounded in real system responses.
do: Prevent harmful duplicate submissions
Show pending feedback in the affected region
Only confirm success after a successful response
Make retries safe and explain whether entered data is retained
avoid: Optimistic success for irreversible or critical tasks without recovery
Infinite spinners and silent failures
verify: Test slow, rejected, cancelled, offline, and duplicate-request scenarios

uxGuidelines.title: Responsive reflow
uxGuidelines.summary: Adapt information architecture and control behavior to available space rather than shrinking a desktop layout indefinitely.
do: Choose breakpoints where content stops working, not by device branding alone
Reflow wide tables, navigation, forms, and action groups deliberately
Preserve task order and state across layout changes
avoid: Fixed widths that cause horizontal page overflow
Removing essential content on mobile
verify: Check narrow, medium, wide, zoomed, and long-content conditions

uxGuidelines.title: Long text and localization resilience
uxGuidelines.summary: Let labels, translations, user names, and user-generated text wrap or truncate with a discoverable recovery path.
do: Allow wrapping for ordinary text and long labels
Clamp only when the full text remains available through a clear action
Test translated strings, long tokens, right-to-left layouts, and browser zoom where applicable
avoid: Fixed-height text containers that clip content
Applying overflow hidden to entire interactive controls
verify: Test 2× label length and realistic localization

uxGuidelines.title: Empty and no-results states
uxGuidelines.summary: Differentiate a new workspace, a truly empty dataset, a filtered no-result state, and a failed request.
do: Explain why the current view is empty
Offer a relevant next action, such as create, clear filters, or retry
Avoid implying failure when there is simply no data
avoid: Using one generic illustration for every empty condition
Providing a create action that does not fit the current permissions
verify: Test initial, filtered, permission-limited, and error states

uxGuidelines.title: Icon and icon-button clarity
uxGuidelines.summary: Icons should reinforce meaning; controls that only show an icon need an accessible name and understandable target.
do: Use a consistent icon family and familiar metaphors where possible
Give icon-only controls a meaningful accessible name
Include text for unfamiliar, ambiguous, or high-consequence actions
avoid: Emoji as a substitute for a coherent product icon set
Same icon meaning different actions in different screens
verify: Inspect screen-reader names and tooltip behavior with keyboard and touch

uxGuidelines.title: Data freshness and units
uxGuidelines.summary: Make time range, source, units, precision, and freshness visible wherever they change interpretation.
do: State the period and timezone for time-based metrics
Label currency, percentages, counts, and measurement units
Distinguish stale, partial, cached, and live data when that affects decisions
avoid: Mixing percentage points with percent change
Showing a timestamp without its meaning or relevant timezone
verify: Compare labels and values after filtering, refresh, and error recovery

uxGuidelines.title: Destructive action protection
uxGuidelines.summary: Scale confirmation to consequence and offer undo or recovery where feasible.
do: Name the affected object and consequence explicitly
Use a confirmation step only when it materially reduces risk
Offer undo or recovery when the system supports it
avoid: Generic 'Are you sure?' prompts without context
Using destructive styling for routine navigation
verify: Test cancel, confirm, permission failure, and repeated activation

uxGuidelines.title: Navigation and orientation
uxGuidelines.summary: Make location, hierarchy, and escape paths consistent so users can move without losing context.
do: Use stable labels and predictable information architecture
Preserve back navigation and state where expected
Support deep links to meaningful locations when the product benefits
avoid: Overloaded top-level menus
Nested overlays without a clear route back
Using color alone for the active location
verify: Start from a deep link, navigate, then use browser or system back

uxGuidelines.title: Action and error wording
uxGuidelines.summary: Use concrete labels that explain what an action does and error messages that help recovery.
do: Use a verb plus an object when the action is ambiguous
Describe what happened, what is affected, and what to do next
Keep status language consistent across toast, button, and page
avoid: Generic 'Oops' without guidance
Button labels like 'Submit' when a more specific label is feasible
Blaming or shaming language

uxGuidelines.title: Operational table usability
uxGuidelines.summary: Tables must support the comparison and row-level tasks that justify their density.
do: Align numbers and label units consistently
Expose sort state accessibly and keep row actions discoverable
Handle narrow screens with deliberate column prioritization or an alternate view
avoid: Using a table for unrelated cards
Color-coded cells without textual explanation
Unlabeled bulk actions
verify: Test long values, no results, sorting, filtering, selection, and keyboard access

uxGuidelines.title: Perceived performance and stability
uxGuidelines.summary: Communicate work in progress while preventing avoidable shifts and blocking interactions.
do: Reserve space for images, embeds, and async content
Lazy-load offscreen media when appropriate and avoid lazy-loading primary visible content
Use a stable skeleton only when it reflects the expected shape
avoid: Layout jumps when fonts or images load
Animating layout properties for routine feedback
Skeletons that look like real data indefinitely
verify: Check a slow connection, reduced motion, and content after failure

chartPatterns.title: Time-series line chart
chartPatterns.summary: Use a line chart to show trend and change over ordered time intervals with clearly stated sampling and scale.
priorities: Label the time range, interval, timezone, and value unit
Use honest axes and clearly indicate missing intervals
Keep tooltips available by keyboard or an accessible data alternative
avoid: Connecting gaps in data as if they were observed values
Changing y-axis range between comparisons without disclosure

chartPatterns.title: Category comparison bar chart
chartPatterns.summary: Use bars to compare discrete categories on a consistent baseline, with labels and units that support quick ranking.
priorities: Sort categories when ranking is the main task
Keep a zero baseline for ordinary bar comparisons unless a justified design is clearly explained
Provide direct value labels when they improve scan speed
avoid: 3D bars and decorative gradients that obscure comparison
Too many categories with unreadable labels

chartPatterns.title: Composition chart
chartPatterns.summary: Use stacked bars or a proportion-focused chart only when the whole and meaningful component relationships are clear.
priorities: State the denominator and period
Keep component colors stable across screens
Use an accessible legend and values for small segments
avoid: Too many slices or nearly indistinguishable colors
Comparing pie angles across many categories when precise comparison matters

chartPatterns.title: Distribution chart
chartPatterns.summary: Use histograms, box plots, or distribution summaries when variability and spread matter more than only the average.
priorities: Explain bin sizes or quartiles when the audience needs them
Include sample size and context for small datasets
Show outliers without implying they are errors by default
avoid: Using a single average to conceal a wide distribution
Comparing distributions with incompatible scales

chartPatterns.title: Uncertainty and data context
chartPatterns.summary: Communicate uncertainty, sampling, source, and data freshness where they change a chart's interpretation.
priorities: Name the metric source and period
Show confidence intervals or uncertainty when relevant and supported
Distinguish measured, estimated, forecast, and incomplete values
avoid: Implying prediction is historical fact
Unsupported confidence percentages or made-up labels

chartPatterns.title: Accessible chart alternative
chartPatterns.summary: Do not make the chart's colors or visual position the only way to retrieve important information.
priorities: Give the chart an informative title and concise summary
Offer a table or downloadable structured data when detailed values matter
Use patterns, labels, line styles, or shape in addition to color
avoid: Legend-only meaning that cannot be understood without sight
Canvas-only chart output with no accessible description

chartPatterns.title: Dashboard chart hierarchy
chartPatterns.summary: Organize charts around a question and decision path rather than maximizing chart count.
priorities: Lead with key status or comparison, then explain contributing factors
Align time ranges and filters across related charts
Provide drill-down to raw or supporting data where appropriate
avoid: Repeated KPI cards with no context
Sparklines without labels when the trend has decision consequences

stackGuides.title: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
stackGuides.summary: Build resilient native interfaces with semantic HTML, scoped CSS, and small stateful modules before reaching for a framework.
priorities: Use native buttons, links, labels, forms, and dialogs when their semantics match
Keep visual tokens in CSS custom properties and behavior in clear modules
Handle focus, error, empty, and loading states directly
avoid: Clickable divs where native controls work
Large inline scripts that mix rendering, data, and event logic without structure
Assuming a CDN dependency is available offline

stackGuides.title: React interface implementation
stackGuides.summary: Use components and state at the scope matching the user-visible behavior, and preserve the application's existing conventions.
priorities: Use stable keys and controlled state where values affect rendering
Keep effects for synchronization, not derived render-time calculations
Extract shared components when there is real repeated behavior
avoid: Duplicated state for values derivable from props/state
Effects that create event-handler loops or fail cleanup
Adding a state library for a small isolated state

stackGuides.title: Next.js and server-rendered React
stackGuides.summary: Choose server and client boundaries deliberately and keep interactive code on the smallest client surface that needs it.
priorities: Use server rendering for appropriate content and data access
Keep secrets and privileged operations off the client
Handle loading, error, metadata, and navigation using the project's router conventions
avoid: Making an entire page client-rendered without need
Exposing secrets in public environment variables
Mixing router-generation conventions from different Next.js versions

stackGuides.title: Vue or Svelte interface
stackGuides.summary: Use the framework's native reactive and component patterns rather than layering a second state model on top.
priorities: Use clear component boundaries and typed or documented props
Keep async state explicit and cleanup subscriptions or event listeners
Follow the project's installed major version and established conventions
avoid: Invented APIs from another framework version
Direct DOM mutation that fights the framework's rendering model

stackGuides.title: Tailwind and component primitives
stackGuides.summary: Use utility classes and existing primitives to express a coherent token system rather than creating unrelated one-off styles.
priorities: Inspect the existing theme configuration and installed version
Centralize semantic color and spacing roles
Reuse accessible primitive behavior before restyling it
avoid: Combining conflicting class utilities unpredictably
Copying a component while dropping keyboard or disabled behavior
Assuming a component library removes the need for accessibility checks

stackGuides.title: React Native and Flutter mobile UI
stackGuides.summary: Map the design to native platform navigation, keyboard, safe area, accessibility, and touch behavior.
priorities: Respect safe areas, keyboard avoidance, and platform navigation patterns
Size controls for touch and provide platform-relevant accessibility labels
Test on realistic screen dimensions and text scale settings
avoid: Applying browser hover assumptions to touch interfaces
Fixed-height layouts that clip dynamic text
Ignoring platform back behavior

stackGuides.title: Three.js and WebGL experiences
stackGuides.summary: Treat the 3D scene as a progressive enhancement with a clear performance and accessibility budget.
priorities: Provide a meaningful fallback and keep essential text in the DOM
Limit draw calls, texture size, and continuously active animation
Pause or reduce motion when hidden or when user preferences request it
avoid: Using the 3D canvas as the only navigation or data interface
Loading a heavy scene before the core page content
Infinite animation that drains mobile resources

stackGuides.title: Framework version and platform constraints
stackGuides.summary: Use code patterns compatible with the installed framework version, build pipeline, and supported platforms.
priorities: Inspect package manifests and lockfiles before selecting APIs
Separate current guidance from legacy APIs and migration advice
Verify platform-specific behavior with the project's own build and tests
avoid: Combining examples from incompatible major versions
Adding dependencies without a clear need
Claiming a build or runtime check was performed when it was not
